Tosafot on Bava Batra 175a:10:1.hebrew: המלוה את חבירו בשטר כו' [על ידי] עדים גובה מנכסים בני חורין - הכא תנן בהדיא דמלוה על פה לא גבי ממשועבדים [מדרבנן]. והא דפרש"י פרק הניזקין (גיטין דף נא. ושם) דמזון האשה והבנות גובין מנכסים בני חורין לפי שאין קצובים, אבל היו קצובים היו גובין אע"פ שאין כתובים משום דהוה כמלוה ע"פ — ליתא. ואגב ריהטא לא עיין בה, אלא טעמא דאכילת פירות למזון האשה והבנות דגבי אם היו קצובים, אפילו אין כתובים, משום דקלא אית להו. והקשה ה"ר יעקב מקורבי"ל: אם כן היאך נשבעין במודה מקצת הטענה? והא אין נשבעין על כפירת שעבוד קרקעות! ואומר רבי: כגון שמחל שעבודו, א"נ בדליכא עדים, דהא דשעבודא דאורייתא היינו על פי עדים, אבל על פי עצמו לא. ובפרק קמא דבבא מציעא (דף ד: ושם) הארכתי יותר מבכאן:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 175a:10:1.english: "One who lends his fellow with a document, etc. [through] witnesses, collects from free property" - Here we learn explicitly that an oral loan is not collected from purchasers of the debtor's property [by rabbinic law]. As for what Rashi explained in chapter Hanizakin (Gittin 51a, see there) — that the sustenance of the wife and daughters is collected from free property because it is not fixed, but if it were fixed, they would collect even if it is not written, since it is like an oral loan — this is incorrect. [Rashi] wrote it in haste and did not examine it closely. Rather, the reason of the eating of fruits [applies] to the sustenance of the wife and daughters: that she collects if they were fixed, even if they are not written, because they have publicity. And Rabbi Yaakov of Corbeil raised a difficulty: If so, how does one take an oath in the case of one who admits to part of the claim? Surely one does not take an oath over the denial of a lien on land! And my teacher says: [It applies] where, for example, he waived his lien; or alternatively, where there are no witnesses, for the principle that a lien is Torah-law applies only when it is established through witnesses, but not through the debtor's own word. And in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (4b, see there) I discussed this at greater length than here:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 175a:3:1.hebrew: ורב ושמואל דאמרי תרוייהו מלוה וכו' - וא"ת: והא דברי שכיב מרע ככתובין וכמסורין דמו, מאחר דאם כתבו ונתנו היו נותנים, השתא אמאי אין נותנים, כמחלק כל נכסיו? וי"ל: לא דמי; דהיכא דנותן מטעם מתנה בודאי תקנו שיהיו ככתובין וכמסורין, שמא תטרף דעתו עליו. אבל מצוה להן ליתן מכח מלוה ולא מטעם אחר, אין לו אלא מכח מלוה כאשר בתחלה, והלכך אין נותנין:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 175a:3:1.english: "And Rav and Shmuel, who both say [that a loan, etc.]" - And if you ask: But the words of a dying person are considered like something written and delivered! Since, if he had written it and given it, they would give [the money], why now do they not give it, just as in the case of one who distributes all his property? And one can answer: It is not comparable; for where he gives on the basis of a gift, the Sages certainly enacted that [his words] be treated as written and delivered, lest his mind become unsettled over it. But [where] he commands them to give on the basis of a loan and not for any other reason, he has nothing except on the basis of a loan, as at the outset, and therefore they do not give.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 175a:4:1.hebrew: הא דמקויים - וא"ת: הא דנקט שטרא מקויים, צריכין למימר דנאמן? ועוד: מה אנו צריכין לנאמנות? ממילא גבי ע"י שטר שבידו! ועוד: למה לי הקדש? ועוד: מאי איריא שכ"מ, דאין אדם חוטא ולא לו, כדמפרש בפ' שום היתומים (ערכין דף כג. ושם) — אפי' בריא נמי? וי"ל, דכולהו איצטריך לגבות בלא שבועה; דאי לא הוה אלא שטרא, הוה בעי שבועה, כדתנן (כתובות דף פז.): הבא ליפרע מנכסים משועבדים, לא יפרע אלא בשבועה. ואפילו הקדש, אי לא שכ"מ ואי לא נאמנותו, הוה [בעי] שבועה, דמה לי משתעבד לגבוה, מה לי משתעבד להדיוט. והכי מפרש בהדיא בפ' שבועת הדיינים (שבועות דף מב:) על הא דקתני (ברייתא): "אבל נשבעים לקטן ולהקדש" — ליפרע מנכסי הקדש. (ופריך): תנינא (כו') מנכסים משועבדים כו'! סד"א הנ"מ הדיוט, אבל הקדש לא חיישינן לקנוניא, קמ"ל. ופריך: והא א"ר הונא שכ"מ כו'! ומשני: דוקא שכ"מ, דאין אדם חוטא ולא לו. ומכאן נראה לרבי הא דמבעיא לן פ' הניזקין (גיטין דף נ:) גבי "אין נפרעין מנכסים משועבדין במקום שיש נכסים בני חורין, אפילו הן זיבורית" — במתנה מאי? בההיא דמנכסים משועבדים לא יפרע אלא בשבועה הוי; ודאי ה"ה מתנה, דנשבעין כשבאין ליפרע ממנו, דפשיטא ליה נמי הכא דמה לי משתעבדי לגבוה, מה לי משתעבדי להדיוט. אלמא, להדיוט בכה"ג בעי שבועה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 175a:4:1.english: "This [case] where it was validated" - And if you ask: Regarding the fact that [the Gemara] mentioned a validated document, do we need to say that he is believed? Furthermore, why do we need [his] credibility? He collects automatically by means of the document in his possession! Furthermore, why do I need [the case of] consecrated property? Furthermore, why specifically a deathbed ill person, given that a person does not sin when it is not to his own benefit, as [the Gemara] explains in the chapter "Shom HaYetomim" (Arakhin 23a and there) — [this would hold] even for a healthy person too? And one can answer: All of these were necessary in order to collect without an oath. For if there were only a document, he would require an oath, as we learned (Ketubot 87a): "One who comes to collect from mortgaged property may collect only with an oath." And even [in the case of] consecrated property — were it not [a case of] a deathbed ill person, and were it not for his credibility, [the claimant] would require an oath, for what difference is it to me whether it is obligated to the Most High or obligated to a layperson? And so it is explained explicitly in the chapter "Shevuat HaDayanim" (Shevuot 42b), on that which [the Baraita] teaches: "But they administer an oath to a minor and to the consecrated property" — [meaning] to collect from the property of the consecrated property. (And [the Gemara] asks): We already learned (etc.) "from mortgaged property," etc.! [The Gemara answers:] One might have thought that this applies only to a layperson, but regarding consecrated property we do not suspect collusion; therefore it teaches us [otherwise]. And [the Gemara] asks: But didn't Rav Huna say [that a] deathbed ill person, etc.! And it answers: Specifically a deathbed ill person, since a person does not sin when it is not to his own benefit. And from here it appears to me [that] regarding that which we are uncertain in the chapter "HaNizakin" (Gittin 50b) concerning "one may not collect from mortgaged property where there is unencumbered property, even if it is of the poorest quality" — [namely,] what is the law with regard to a gift? In that case, which is like [the law of] "from mortgaged property he may collect only with an oath," certainly the same applies to a gift, that they administer an oath when they come to collect from him; for it is also obvious to him here that what difference is it to me whether it is obligated to the Most High or obligated to a layperson. Evidently, in such a case, with regard to a layperson, he requires an oath:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 175a:4:2.hebrew: הא דלא מקויים - וא"ת: כי היכי דאי לא מקויים [אמרינן] שהוא מזוייף, והאב אמר שלא להשביע את בניו — בהא נמי לימא "שלא להשביע את בניו", ופרוע הוא, ומדברי האב אין ראיה? ואין לומר דא"כ היו נותנים על ידי שבועה אם היה מקויים, שא"צ אלא לישבע שלא נפרע, וזה יכול הוא לעשות, ולא שייך לומר אין נותנים. אבל בלא מקויים, דבעי קיום [קודם שיפרע], שייך לומר אין נותנים. דהא גבי הקדש אמרו: נאמן במקויים, ולא טענינן ליה פרוע ויצטרך שבועה, אלא נאמן בלא שבועה, כדמוכח ההיא דשבועות (דף מב:) שהבאתי לעיל. אלא נראה לרבי דהיכא דנקט ההוא מלוה שטרא ומקיים, אין הלוה רגיל לעולם לומר "שלא להשביע" שחייב לו מנה כמו שכתב בשטר, היכא דפרעיה, שלא יהא סבורים העולם שלא פרעו:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 175a:4:2.english: This, that it is not authenticated - And if you ask: Just as, if it is not authenticated, [we say] that it is forged, and the father said [it] so as not to make his sons swear — here too, let us say [that he said it] "so as not to make his sons swear," and [the debt] has been paid, and so there is no proof from the father's words? And one cannot answer that, if so, they would be paying out [the debt] by means of an oath if it were authenticated; for [the borrower] would need only to swear that he had not repaid, and this he is able to do, and it would not be relevant to say that they do not pay. But in the case of a non-authenticated [document], which requires authentication [before it is repaid], it is relevant to say that they do not pay. For regarding [a debt owed to] the Temple treasury, they said: [The debtor] is believed [to admit the debt] when [the document] is authenticated, and we do not make the claim against him that it has been paid, such that he would need an oath; rather, he is believed without an oath, as is proven from that [passage] in Shevuot (42b), which I brought above. Rather, it appears to the Rabbi that where that creditor holds the document and has authenticated it, the debtor is never accustomed to say "so as not to make [his sons] swear" that he owes him a maneh as written in the document, when he has [in fact] repaid him, so that people will not think that he did not repay him:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 175a:7:1.english: "Rather, if it was stated, etc." - He does not want to say [it that way]; rather, the opposite was stated, since he knows the received tradition regarding one who said "A maneh to so-and-so is in my possession," that they are believed:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 175a:7:2.hebrew: חזר ואמר לנו אבא פרעתי נאמנים דלמא אדכורי מדכר - היינו פרעתי קודם לכן [כדקאמר דלמא] אדכורי מדכר, [היינו] באותה שעה, כדמוכח בסמוך [דקאמר] "אי איתא דפרעיה" כו'. והכא נאמנים משום שהוא היה נאמן לומר "פרעתי קודם לכן" מגו דנאמן לומר "פרעתי אחרי כן", כדתנן: "מנה לי בידך", א"ל: "הן", למחר א"ל: "תנהו לי", "נתתיו לך" — פטור; אלא דמשביעין אותו שבועת היסת מדרבנן, ואף הם יכולים לומר: "פרענו אחרי כן". והא דאמר אין נאמנים כיון דלא פסקה למילתיה, היינו דטפי מסתבר לומר שם אין נאמנין "מתנו מנה לפלוני". ואומר רבי: הא דאמר סוף פ"ק דגיטין (דף יד.) "הנהו גנאי דעבוד חושבנא בהדי הדדי כו' לסוף לא פש גביה ולא מידי", ומסיק דהאי דאקני למריה ארעא זוזי דפשו גביה, קנין בטעות הוא, וחוזר. ומפרש ר"ת ורבינו חננאל שהיו הן מודים שטעו תחלה בחשבון, שאם לא כן לא היה נאמן, שא"כ אין לך קנין מועיל לעולם, שיאמר "טעיתי", וגם יאמר היאך טעה. הא לאו הוכחה היא, דודאי הוא יכול להיות נאמן בכמה מקומות מגו דהוה מצי למימר "פרעתי אחרי כן", כדאשכחן הכא. אלא נראה דלא מיבעיא שנאמן לומר שטעה כשאמר "מנה לפלוני בידי", אלא הוא נאמן לומר "פרעתי כבר" מגו דמצי למימר "פרעתי אחרי כן". ומ"מ יכול הוא להיות דהתם צריך שיהו מודים שטעה אחרי כן, משום דקנין חשוב כ"תנו" דהכא, דאי פרעיה לא הוה אמר "תנו", ומה לי לשקר — במקום עדים הוא. ה"נ התם, אי איתא דטעה דלא פש גביה מידי, לא הוה מקני. וי"מ דדוקא בשכ"מ שייך למימר אדכורי מדכר, שאין דעתו מיושבת עליו, אבל בריא לא:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 175a:7:2.english: [If they said:] "He went back and said to us: Father said, 'I paid'" — they are believed, since perhaps he remembered - That is, [he said] "I paid" before that [time], [as it says] "perhaps" he remembered — that is, at that time, as is proven shortly after [where it says], "If it were so that he had paid him," etc. And here they are believed because he himself would have been believed to say "I paid before that," by virtue of the fact that he would be believed to say "I paid afterward," as we learned in the Mishnah: [If one says,] "I have a maneh against you," and [the other] said to him, "Yes," and the next day he said to him, "Give it to me," and [the other] said, "I already gave it to you" — he is exempt; except that they administer to him a heset oath, rabbinically, and they too can say, "We paid afterward." And as for what [the Gemara] said, that they are not believed, since he did not complete his statement — that is because it is more reasonable to say there that they are not believed, [in the case of] "Give a maneh to so-and-so." And the Rabbi says: Regarding what is said at the end of the first chapter of Gittin (14a): "Those partners who did an accounting with each other, etc. In the end nothing remained with him" — and [the Gemara] concludes that this [case] where he transferred ownership of land to his master for the coins that remained with him, is a transaction made in error, and he may retract. And Rabbeinu Tam and Rabbeinu Chananel explain that they [the partners] admit that they erred at first in the accounting; for if not, he would not be believed, since otherwise there would never be an effective transfer of ownership, as he could say, "I erred," and could even say how he erred. But this is not proof, for certainly he can be believed in many places by virtue of a migo, since he could have said, "I paid afterward," as we find here. Rather, it appears that not only is he believed to say that he erred when he said, "A maneh to so-and-so is in my hands," but he is believed to say, "I already paid," by virtue of the fact that he could have said, "I paid afterward." In any case, it may be that there one needs them to admit that he erred afterward, because a transfer of ownership is considered like [the statement] "Give" here: for if he had paid him, he would not have said "Give," and what would he gain by lying? It is in the presence of witnesses. So too there, if it were so that he had erred, [and] nothing remained with him, he would not have made the transfer. And some explain that it applies to say "perhaps he remembered" only with a deathly ill person, whose mind is not settled, but not with a healthy person.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 175a:9:1.hebrew: ודברי שכ"מ ככתובין וכמסורין דמו כו' - האי ״ככתובין״ לא הוי ככתובין דלעיל פ' מי שמת (בבא בתרא דף קנא.), דהתם קאמר שהם ככתובים וכמסורין כבר, דלא בעי קנין. אבל הכא לא בעי למימר דדוקא ככתובין וכמסורין, אלא אלימו טובא כדברים הכתובים; הלכך הוי כאילו אמר ״כתבו״. והרבה יפוי כח עשו חכמים בשכיב מרע בלא ההוא דלעיל דלא בעי קנין, כי ההיא דאמר בפרק קמא דגיטין (דף יד:): דהולך כזכי בשכיב מרע, אפילו לא הוי בבריא כזכי:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 175a:9:1.english: "The words of a person on his deathbed are considered as if written and delivered," etc. - This "as if written" is not the same as the "as if written" above in the chapter Mi Shemet (Bava Batra 151a), for there it says that [his words] are as if already written and delivered, so that no act of acquisition (kinyan) is needed. But here it does not mean to say that it is precisely "as if written and delivered"; rather, [his words] are very powerful, like written words. Therefore it is as if he had said, "Write [it]." And the Sages enacted many strengthenings of legal force for a person on his deathbed, apart from that one above, that no kinyan is needed. Like that which is stated in the first chapter of Gittin (14b): that [the word] "holekh" ("go [and deliver]") is like "zekhi" ("acquire") for a person on his deathbed, even though for a healthy person it would not be like "zekhi."
